## Client books arrive open, and you can't show they didn't change {#your-seat}

<span class="kicker">From your seat</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>Rebuilding every month</h3><p>Matching Stripe payouts to charges by hand, and chasing clients by email.</p></div>
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>No proof of what didn't change</h3><p>You can show today's books, not that they match what you reviewed.</p></div>
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>Seats cost your clients</h3><p>QuickBooks caps users, so adding you can force a client up a plan.</p></div>
</div>

Sources: `docs/brand/trifold-brand-and-messaging.md`, "Ideal customer profiles" 4 (bookkeeper or CPA partner serving 10–100 small businesses; cares about clean reconciliation to Stripe, exports, an audit trail, fewer client emails, recurring revenue); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §2 (manual close; books changed quietly); `docs/business/market-research.md` §2 and §3 point 2 (QuickBooks user caps 1 / 3 / 5 / 25: "a school that adds its CPA or a second admin has to upgrade").

## Trifold grows through accounting firms: three tiers, no referral fees {#firm-tiers}

<span class="kicker">The firm program · the main channel · proposed</span>

<div class="tiers">
<div class="tier"><span class="riser">1 client</span><div class="tread"><h3>Listed</h3><span class="rate">$0</span><p>Free seats; clients get 20% off year one. First 5 firms: co-design partners</p></div></div>
<div class="tier"><span class="riser">5 clients</span><div class="tread"><h3>Practice</h3><span class="rate">$99/mo</span><p>30% off client plans; one bill; Rifo batch close (next)</p></div></div>
<div class="tier"><span class="riser">15 clients · later</span><div class="tread"><h3>Practice Pro</h3><span class="rate">$399/mo</span><p>Your prices, wholesale: Pro $49; Audited $99 once it ships</p></div></div>
</div>

<p class="fine">The channel: 46,000–52,000 US CPA firms; about 30,700 UK accounting enterprises (sourced).</p>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> Drafts; nothing built yet. Practice Pro opens after about 100 paying clients.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §2, "Firm tiers" (Listed at 1 active client, $0, free firm seats, clients 20% off their first year, directory listing; Practice at 5, $99/mo + 30% off each client's plan, one firm bill, a dashboard across clients, books templates, Rifo closing months in a batch; Practice Pro at 15 or pay to unlock, $399/mo + wholesale per client, e.g. Pro $49, Witnessed $99 (renamed Audited by the owner, 2026-11-07), the firm's own prices and checkout, branded portal, white-label verify page with the badge kept), "Build order", and the header ("Nothing in this doc is built"). No referral fees: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §4c and go-to-market §3.3. The 20% first-year discount is a placeholder (pricing-strategy §11 item 5). Firm counts: `docs/business/market-research.md` §6.6 (US 46,000–52,000 CPA firms, CPA Trendlines 2024; UK 30,705 accounting and auditing enterprises, SIC 69201, ONS via a secondary compilation; sourced). Owner decision of 2026-11-07: accounting firms are a key enabler; about 5 firms join in Stage A as co-design partners (Listed plus a written agreement), Practice comes in Stage B, Practice Pro in Stage C after about 100 paying clients.
:::

## You earn your own markup: an example firm keeps about $7,000 a month {#what-you-earn}

<span class="kicker">Economics · illustrative</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><h3>The example</h3><p>30 schools on Practice Pro, each paying the firm $300 a month for bookkeeping and software.</p></div>
<div class="card card--green"><span class="big">≈ $7,000</span><p>a month the firm keeps</p></div>
<div class="card card--ink"><span class="big">≈ $2,050</span><p>a month to Trifold, at about $55 wholesale a client</p></div>
</div>

<p class="fine">White label stops at the proof: every receipt keeps its "Verify at trifold…" link. Clients own their books and can leave with them.</p>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> Draft wholesale prices and an assumed $300 fee.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §2 ("Example": 30 schools on Practice Pro at $300/mo; average wholesale about $55, mostly Pro at $49, a few Witnessed (now Audited) at $99; Trifold ≈ 30 × $55 + $399 ≈ $2,050/mo; the firm keeps ≈ $7,000/mo; "White label stops at the proof": the verify link and "Witnessed by Trifold" can't be removed), §3.3 (the firm earns its own markup, not a fee from Trifold), §5 (a departing firm: the school owns its books, export never paywalled). "Witnessed by Trifold" appears only on records with a valid Trifold witness signature (`TRADEMARKS.md`); the witness is not built.
:::

## Idaho and Utah allow referral fees with disclosure; Trifold pays none {#idaho-utah}

<span class="kicker">Compliance · not legal advice</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>Banned when…</h3><p>The firm also does an audit, review or attest work for that client, or a compilation a third party relies on, during the engagement. No contingent fee for preparing a return.</p></div>
<div class="card card--green"><h3>Otherwise…</h3><p>Allowed with written disclosure of the amount or its basis, before the referral.</p></div>
</div>

<p class="fine">Trifold pays accountants no cash, a choice stricter than either state's law, so your independence stays clean.</p>

::: {.notes}
Source: `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §4, "Paying accountants: what Idaho and Utah allow". Idaho: Code §54-218 and IDAPA 24.30.01.200 (banned with an attest service, or a compilation a third party will use that doesn't disclose a lack of independence; disclosure in writing, clear and conspicuous, stating the amount or basis, before the referral). Utah: Code §58-26a-502 (banned with an audit or review, such a compilation, or an examination of prospective financial information; a commission disclosed to the person referred, a referral fee to the client). Both: the ban lasts for the engagement plus the period the statements cover; no contingent fee for preparing a tax return. Not checked: enrolled agents (Circular 230), other states (Florida is stricter), AICPA Rule 1.520. A lawyer reviews the terms before launch.
:::

## Work on a client's own install today; one install for many clients needs an agreement {#firms-and-fsl}

<span class="kicker">License</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--green"><h3>Allowed today</h3><p>Self-hosting tfd for your own books, and working on a client's own install.</p></div>
<div class="card card--clay"><h3>Needs an agreement</h3><p>One tfd your firm runs for many clients. Use the hosted firm program, or ask for a partner agreement.</p></div>
</div>

<p class="fine">Whether to add a public grant for firms is undecided; it is settled before the program launches.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §4c, "Firms hosting tfd for their clients" (FSL allows professional services on a client's own install; one tfd for many clients is probably a Competing Use; options A–D; suggestion A now with D on request; any permission is a separate written grant, never an edited FSL); `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §2 (the program is option D made public); AGENTS.md "Open licensing items" 2. The engine is FSL-1.1-ALv2 (AGENTS.md "Licensing").
:::
